subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment with your infra team: 

Call recap (short):
- Goal: Private connectivity for Redwood Private integration (model inference + embeddings service) into FinPay VPC.
- Primary requirements you called out: private endpoints (no public egress for requests), IP allowlist for outbound traffic, DNS resolution to private endpoints, and mTLS for service-to-service authentication.
- Integration scope: SDK setup (auth + client config), structured output/tool-calling considerations for secure data routing, and embeddings/reranker wiring for your vector store.

Immediate next steps:
1) We will share a VPC connectivity checklist and a sample firewall rules CSV (attached) for your network team.
2) Marissa (cc'd) will run an infra deep-dive: she can review IPs, routing, and mTLS options with your networking/security engineers.
3) Please confirm whether FinPay requires source-NAT (SNAT) for outbound traffic and whether you have static egress IPs we should expect.
4) If you can send the current allowlist and any proxy/firewall appliance details, that will speed things up.

Attachments: vpc_connectivity_checklist.pdf (attached)

Proposed times for infra deep-dive (PST): Fri 3/26 10:00-11:00 or Mon 3/29 09:00-10:00. Let us know what works.

Thanks — excited to get this into a short mutual action plan.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: FinPay Networking Team <networking@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Thanks Lauren — helpful recap. Some answers and a few follow-ups from our side: 

Answers / constraints:
- We do prefer private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / Interface VPC endpoints) for any managed service integration.
- Our egress is SNATed behind a NAT gateway today; we can provide the static egress IPs for outbound flows. Expect ~3 public egress IPs for the account.
- We require mTLS for inbound service-to-service calls to any private endpoint. We manage client certs via our internal PKI; if Redwood can support client cert validation + CA pinning that would be ideal.
- DNS: we leverage a private Route53 zone; we need the service hostname(s) you expose so our DNS team can create conditional forwarding/routing.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can your SDK be configured to point at a private endpoint address/hostname (non-public) and accept client certs for mTLS?
2) For embeddings and rerankers, is traffic to the embeddings endpoint also proxied over the same private path, and is data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys?
3) What are the expected outbound IP addresses or ranges we should allow for callbacks/health checks (if any)?

We'll get you the static egress IPs and our firewall list by EOD. Also looping in our infra lead Maria (networking@finpay.com) for the deep-dive.

— Alex Johnson
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Alex — thanks for the quick answers and for looping your infra lead. I put together a short technical note and attachments that should help your networking/security team prepare. Attaching: vpc_diagram.png, firewall_rules.csv (sample), plus the checklist Lauren referenced.

Quick answers up front:
- Private endpoints: Yes — Redwood Private supports AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect. Our SDKs can be configured to point at a private hostname (we'll provide the FQDNs and IPs once the endpoint is provisioned).
- mTLS: Supported. For Redwood Private deployments we can require client certificate authentication for inbound connections to the private control plane and inference endpoints. We support validating client cert chains signed by your internal CA and can pin issuer fingerprints.
- Embeddings/rerankers: All inference traffic (generation, embeddings, rerank) can be routed over the same private network path; embeddings storage is encrypted at rest. For enterprise/private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys — let us know if you want that enabled.
- Outbound/callback IPs: For hosted fallbacks we have shared egress ranges (will provide) — but for Dedicated/Private there is no public outbound unless you enable egress to the internet. If you require callbacks, we can also set up a static egress NAT behind your VPC peering or PrivateLink endpoint.

Sample firewall rules (see attached CSV):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to REDWOOD-PRIVATE-ENDPOINT-SVC (private IPs) from your application subnets.
- Allow inbound mTLS from your client cert CIDR if you will route through a bastion / proxy.
- DNS: create conditional forwarder for *.redwood-private.internal to our private DNS resolver endpoint or add Route53 private zone delegation as appropriate.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- FinPay: share static egress IPs and current firewall appliance config (Maria).
- Redwood (Marissa): share the endpoint FQDNs, the CA trust bundle we expect for client cert validation, and a small example of SDK auth config and init code.
- Schedule: I can host a 60-minute infra deep-dive Wed 3/31 09:00-10:00 PST or Fri 4/2 11:00-12:00 PST. Please confirm which works for your team.

Note: attaching a lightweight SDK snippet (in the checklist PDF) demonstrating how to configure the client to use a private hostname, attach a client cert for mTLS, and enable structured output (tool-calling) flags so you can test end-to-end routing during the deep-dive.

Let me know if you want me to open a temporary sandbox endpoint for testing - we can provision that and give you short-lived certs.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Integrations
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
